nodes.summary: (a) Every nonempty compact convex subset of a complete metrizable locally convex topological vector space over $\mathbb{R}$ is an absolute retract. (b) Every nonempty compact subset of a pseudometric space that is convex in the sense of Wilson is an absolute retract.
nodes.title: Eilenberg's theorem on compact convex absolute retracts

nodes.summary: A topological space $K$ is an absolute retract when $K$ is compact and, for every separable metrizable space $X$ and every topological embedding $e \colon K \to X$, there is a continuous map $r \colon X \to K$ with $r(e(k)) = k$ for all $k \in K$.
nodes.title: Absolute retract

nodes.summary: A subset $K$ of a pseudometric space $X$ with distance $d$ is convex in the sense of Wilson when for all $x, y \in K$ and every real $t$ with $0 \le t \le 1$ there is exactly one $z \in K$ with $d(x, z) = t \, d(x, y)$ and $d(z, y) = (1 - t) \, d(x, y)$.
nodes.title: Wilson convexity
